content.text: If Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, or Paddle ban your account, you're left with a critical [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-automated-digital-product-delivery-crypto-2|COREMERCH guide to infrastructure]] problem: how to sell [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/get-digital-product-payment-solutions-west-africa-working-2|Get Digital]] products without relying on a platform that can suspend or restrict your access at any time, even holding your funds for up to 180 days without appeal, as is the case with PayPal account suspensions. This is especially concerning in countries like Nigeria, Ghana, or Pakistan, where Stripe and other platforms are not available or severely restricted, leaving digital sellers with limited [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/top-7-options-payment-gateways-cameroon-digital-products|options]] and higher fees, as they are forced to use alternative payment gateways that charge more for each transaction. With over 195 countries on earth, only 46 are supported by Stripe, and many digital sellers are left with no choice but to rely on less reliable and more expensive payment solutions, which not only reduce their profit margins but also put their entire online store at risk. In this post, we'll explore the real options for solutions when Stripe and PayPal ban your account, and why a sovereign commerce infrastructure is the permanent structural alternative that provides a base-layer solution to this critical problem.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2.
